review: Reviewed Wren's round-363 request (Hand frapping of a crossing lashing: improve the sliding resistance of an actual branch-crossing lashing by drawing its existing turns together with transverse frapping turns, if physically feasible, with measured inspection, bounded hand trials and reversible untying; her two-turn lashing of two 31.6 mm branches held 10 N separation for 60 s but slipped at 4.3 N in a 5 N slide trial and was untied, recovering both branches and the 0.64 m reed cord, whose assembly had needed up to 0.6124 m; owned pieces and cord only, more cord not assumed, costs to be specified, no presumed strength, slip resistance, safe load or reward) and the World Agent's develop review (learning 3): a general Hand-frap crossing lashings operation by bindingId or a proposed crossing (pieceIds, cordId, crossingAngle, wrapCount), frapCount 1-3, modes assess, attempt, inspect, trial, untie and cancel; minimal mechanism: transverse turns of the existing continuous cord between the crossed pieces round the turn bundle, closed again by the existing overhand, with separate and joined frapping cords outside this version; reuse of the hand-lash-crossing@1, hand-bind-crossing@1 and cord laws without claiming them; study 3 rounds at 0.2; assess 0.5 (positioning, route measurement and clearance, nothing tied); inspect 0.2; attempt frapCount + 3 paid rounds of 0.5 (measure and plan, release the closure while supporting the turns, route and snug each transverse turn, close/dress/release-check) with its own measurement and a measured shortfall stopping before the closure opens; trial 0.5 with 0 < force <= 10 N and 0 < duration <= 60 s, slide or separate; full untie frapCount + wrapCount + 1 rounds of 0.5; free cancel; required length as the longest stage including travel, offsets, closure, tails and passing slack; a versioned transverse-contact law computing paths, per-turn tension and transferred squeeze from geometry with the bounded 5 N pull and capstan losses at cord-on-cord and cord-on-bark contacts, no strength bonus; conservation, pause, resume, relaxation, cancel, death and wear once per cord; no reward, rating or shelter. The specification is self-consistent and every gated transition has an explicit rule, so this is a simplified real mechanism, not a first release. Implemented hand-frap-crossing@1 in scope long-ex16 (new module packages/world-core/src/long-crossing-frapping.ts, export LONG_CROSSING_FRAPPING, handler long.hand-frap-crossing, events prefixed crossing-frapping-, law transverse-contact@1, method same-cord-transverse-turns-overhand-closure, cord processing key crossingFrapping), registered at the end of V7_PACKAGES with dependencies foundation-open@1, hand-twist-fiber-cord@1, hand-tie-cord-knot@1, hand-join-fiber-cords@1, hand-bind-crossing@1 and hand-lash-crossing@1; learning 3 at 0.2 energy per paid study round, no prerequisite, empty references (exact ids only), ability text 3,110 code units within 3,500. Modes and costs: assess (frapCount with bindingId of an own dressed lashing, or with own pieceIds, cordId, crossingAngle 30-90 and wrapCount 2-4 validated by the lashing's own piece and cord rules) spends 0.5 and changes no item; attempt (bindingId of an own dressed, free lashing, frapCount) reserves the three items and pays frapCount + 3 rounds of 0.5 through workPay, resumable only by attempt with workId; inspect (bindingId of a frapped lashing or workId) 0.2; trial 0.5; untie pays frapCount + wrapCount + 1 rounds (withdraw-closure-end, unwrap-frap-n..1, unwrap-turn-n..1); cancel is free. Before any cost: mastery, arguments, exact own items, a dressed lashing not held by work or already frapped, friction laws, cord condition at least 0.5, tails of at least the 0.02 m pinch, room, footing, bystanders, energy and a visible least length (the lashing's seated length and tails, twice the top piece's diameter to reach the contact plane and back, and per transverse turn twice the thinner piece's diameter plus a full turn round a cord-width disc at its stacking offset); refusals spend nothing; no material is consumed or added. Modeling assumptions of transverse-contact@1: the base turns are the live multi-turn-contact@1 plan of the lashing; each turn's two legs (its hull sides) are cut at the contact plane of the pieces and drawn in within the turn plane along the obtuse bisector, the drawn path being the exact tangents from the drawn point to both offset sections plus their arcs (ellipse radius a^2 b^2 / q^3 + w/2), collision-free by construction, with the room limited where the drawn point meets a section; in plan the wedge zone is where a sphere of the cord width cannot clear both pieces (under the top piece, over the bottom one), found on 360 rays; the transverse route is the shortest found closed curve enclosing both leg bundles (discs of radius w round each leg at the contact plane) and the wedge zone whose radius never falls below R = max(bend limit, w/2), the boundary of C + disc(R) with C grown greedily from the crossing (it may slightly overstate the length), its straight runs subdivided every millimetre and lifted only as far as the gap requires, its 3D length measured and its clearance and leg gap verified (otherwise route-intersects; no bearing on a bundle is blocked-gap); later transverse turns lie on earlier ones one width further out with a radial step of one width as their advance; the end leaves the outer turn's crown beside it and runs down that plane's hull to the contact plane and back up beside the transverse turns over the bridge to the closure (back up = down + bridge + frapCount x w), the other end keeps its bridge, the overhand is re-formed with the lashing's closure, forming, pinch and tail rules and the tails share the rest equally; stages are release-closure, route-frap-k (base turns with any creep slack, travel, transverse turns so far, 0.04 m passing slack and two pinches), forming the closure and seating with two 0.02 m + w tails, the need being their maximum; one hand closes round the crossing and its turns within the inherited 0.1 m span while the other pushes the end through the wedge passages, finger room there not otherwise modeled and no lift needed; each transverse turn is snugged with the cord-bend@1 5 N pull at its exit and its tension falls back round it by the capstan relation (0.3 cord on cord over the leg bundles and earlier turns, 0.3 cord on bark in the wedge) over the crossing-contact@1 bridging share rho/R, earlier turns keeping their own snugged tension; the force on each bundle is the cord's tension difference across the normal directions it carries, its inward part pushing the bundle, while wedge forces go into the pieces and change no turn tension (wedging the pieces apart is not represented, which understates); both bundles' legs are drawn in together and each turn's tension rises by the fiber-cord@1 stiffness x lengthening / turn length as a uniform increment, as multi-turn-contact@1 takes loads (friction redistribution along the turn is not represented), so creep slack is taken up first, each side balancing where the sum of leg tension x d(length)/d(draw) equals its push and a bundle stopping where it meets the pieces; the frapped model is the lashing's model with that increment written as a negative creep loss, so the inherited tension, separate and slide trial, closure, breaking, creep and wear rules apply unchanged; the drawn-in route is remeasured, lengthening the tails; the release check needs the closure's slip load above end 1 and above the larger of the outer turn's end tension and the 5 N exit at end 2, tails of 0.02 m + w and a peak below the curvature-adjusted breaking force, otherwise the closure slips and every turn falls loose or the cord parts into two owned fragments of conserved fiber and length; the tension transfer where the end passes from the outer turn to the transverse turns is not resolved and is reported, with wedging and friction redistribution, as unvalidated mechanics; transverse turns keep their dressed tension in trials and do not creep. Effects and relation: the three items stay one conserved relation under the lashing's id; while the closure is open the lashing record is in state frapping and the cord takes its prior role, once frapped the state is frapped and the cord takes the bound role, so hand-lash-crossing@1 no longer treats it as its own lashing (its trial, untie, inspect and attempt refuse it and its environment skips it), hand-bind-crossing@1's bound-role wear of 0.0005 per round applies exactly once (fiber-cord@1's while open in the hands), and the frapped cord parts in place between rounds if it can no longer carry its own tension. A closed lashing pauses uncharged on low energy, no action or blocked room; turns open in the hands fall loose when not worked, carried away, cancelled or at death, freeing all three items (rebuilding is hand-lash-crossing work); the inherited jam and condition rule makes a closure resist opening for a paid round; death leaves the items where the person died once; nothing is refunded. Events crossing-frapping-assessed, -started, -measured, -shortfall, -resisted, -closure-released, -turn-routed, -turn-snugged, -release-held, -release-failed, -relaxed, -paused, -resumed, -cancelled, -stopped, -inspected, -trial, -grip-slipped, -crossing-slipped, -closure-slipped, -damaged, -broken, -loosened, -closure-withdrawn, -frap-unwrapped, -turn-unwrapped and -untied are emitted only when they occur, with reusable schematic view metadata (component crossing-frapping reusing the crossing-lashing, crossing-binding, fiber-cord and cord-knot views: item and work ids, stage, crossing angle and pose, base turn centrelines, transverse centrelines, counts, closure state, slack, migration, draw-in, condition, evidence and unvalidated mechanics; an assessment or shortfall carries a distinguished measured-route overlay with the numerical shortfall and a completed appearance follows only the passed release check); visualComponents is empty. Inspection reports visible state only. Verified personal records are keyed by material, width, piece sizes, angle, turn and transverse counts and outcome (trials add condition band, force and duration), so identical results are no new information; inspection is unverified; release-held carries no qualified flag, and no reward, satisfaction, shelter effect or rating is added. Measured on the paused state: Wren's actual 0.64 m, 5.9 mm cord lashed in two turns at 90 degrees round two 31.6 mm branch units needs 0.8911, 1.1025 and 1.351 m for one, two and three transverse turns (limiting stage forming the closure), short by 0.2511, 0.4625 and 0.711 m, and the visible least of 0.7477 m for one turn refuses attempt before costs, so her paid assessment is the informative precursor and no hand-twisted cord fits; with a 1.2 m, 4.3 mm fixture cord lengthened in place at conserved volume one transverse turn (0.1466 m planned, 0.1331 m drawn in) pushes the bundles with 6.2 and 5.3 N, draws the legs in 3.6 and 3.1 mm and raises each base turn by 4.1 N (leg tensions from 3.3 and 1.3 N to 7.4 and 5.4 N), its 9.1 N end tension below the 34.9 N closure slip load and the 18.1 N breaking force, and the same lashing that slips at 4.5 N unfrapped holds a 10 N slide with a computed slip load of 12.3 N; at 30 degrees the wedge where the gap is below the cord width reaches about 3 cm along the acute bisector, so the route bears on the bark there. Reuse: hand-lash-crossing@1 through a new append-only MULTI_TURN_CONTACT export (planner, tensions, separate and slide rules, creep, fragments, relation and ownership helpers; its ability text and behavior unchanged); hand-bind-crossing@1 through CROSSING_CONTACT, hand-twist-fiber-cord@1 through FIBER_CORD, hand-tie-cord-knot@1 through CORD_KNOT and hand-join-fiber-cords@1 through CORD_BEND; cords made by hand-twist-sectioned-cord@1 are ordinary cords; all reused abilities stay byte-identical. Tests in apps/simulator/test/long-ex16-hand-frap-crossing.test.ts cover scope, dependencies, byte-identical reuse, the size limit and wording, the three paid study rounds, Wren's measured shortfall and pre-cost refusal, the route, offsets and stage geometry, the blocked wedge at 30 degrees, the paid attempt and its draw-in effect, trials, zero slack at the exact length, creep slack taken up, a slipping closure on a stiffer reed fixture, a worn cord breaking while dressing and in place, untying, pause, resume, relaxation and cancel, inspection, single wear, owner-only rules, pre-cost refusals and death.
